reader.requirement: At --std 85 the OBJECT-COMPUTER computer-name must be a system-name (a COBOL word of at most 30 characters from A-Z, 0-9, hyphen, hyphen not first or last, not a 1985 reserved word, never LENGTH/RANDOM/SUM), refused otherwise, accepted when legal, including when the 1985 MEMORY SIZE / PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE / SEGMENT-LIMIT clauses follow it.

edition-consulted.switches: the reserved-word set per edition (R85 column at --std 85)
token-level reservation gate at the edition
COBOL0901 for a word reserved at the edition
clauses without a computer-name gated as computer-name-optional-2002

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: the reserved-word set (MEMORY, WORDS, MODULES, SEGMENT-LIMIT reserved at 85), the 30-character limit, the character set
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb830 and pb3133 accept a legal computer-name with the 1985 clauses; no witness exercises an illegal computer-name

EXIT 65; COBOL0901 'MEMORY' is a reserved word in COBOL-85 (WORDS, MODULES, SEGMENT-LIMIT likewise)
EXIT 65; COBOL1970 '"IBM-370"' is not a clause (370 likewise)
EXIT 0 RAN (OBJECT-COMPUTER. TYPEDEF MEMORY SIZE 8000 WORDS SEGMENT-LIMIT IS 20.)
EXIT 0 RAN (30-character name; 31 refused in c2-31chars)

reader.notes: Same mechanism as SOURCE-COMPUTER: computerName is cobolWord under the edition's reservation gate, word-length limit and character screen; every illegal computer-name probe was refused and every legal one ran. The seed sites in SpecialNamesBinder and characterClassificationClause are not on this rule's path.
reader.at-2023: MEMORY accepted at 2023 (not reserved there); MOVE refused at every edition

refuter.evidence: This fails the same way as SOURCE-COMPUTER, through the same computerName rule. §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.2 makes computer-name, implementor-name and language-name disjoint sets within an implementation (cite.py: OK  §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.2  (4.2.2.1.2 System-Names)  the text is in the clause; OK  §1985:VI.4.4.3 SR1  (4.4.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1). Probes at --std 85 (refute-1985-049/src/sysn/o-*.cob): OBJECT-COMPUTER. CONSOLE. / SYSIN. / SYSOUT. / SYSERR. / C01. / CSP. / EBCDIC. / ASCII. / SWITCH-1. / UPSI-0. all give EXIT 0 RAN. These are this implementation's own implementor-names (ImplementorNames.cs, ImplementorCodeNames.cs). r2-console-both2.cob (OBJECT-COMPUTER. CONSOLE. beside CONSOLE IS MYCON) gives EXIT 0 RAN. All 350 words of the 1985 reserved-word list compiled as the OBJECT-COMPUTER computer-name (src/w85/o-*.cob) were refused with EXIT 65, so the reserved-word part holds.
edition-sites-missed: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4#computerName: no screen against the implementor system-name table; 1985 needs the disjointness arm that 2023 (§8.3.2.3.1, computer-name not in the exclusive list) does not
refuter.corrected: PARTIAL (harm: under-rejects; cause a/c). At --std 85, OBJECT-COMPUTER. EBCDIC. (or CONSOLE, SYSIN, C01, SWITCH-1, and the rest) compiles and runs, although under §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.2 an implementor-name of the implementation cannot also be a computer-name. Expected a refusal at 85. At --std 2023 it is accepted, correctly. Known note: none; the sibling is PB5482.

adjudication.reason: `SOURCE-COMPUTER. CONSOLE.` runs in a program that also uses CONSOLE as an implementor-name; 1985 makes the computer-names and the implementor-names of an implementation disjoint sets. The checker rates this medium: the sentence is about the implementation's name sets, not a syntax rule on programs.
